**Use layout for spacing.** Lay out sibling groups with flex or grid and `gap` instead of per-element margins, which collapse or double without warning. Keep a side gutter of at least 16px at every width, written `padding-left: max(16px, env(safe-area-inset-left, 0px))` and `padding-right: max(16px, env(safe-area-inset-right, 0px))` so that it also clears a system bar at the phone's side: set it once on `body` or one outer wrapper (where colored bands span the width, on each band's inner wrapper), whose vertical padding uses `padding-block` and never a `padding` shorthand that zeroes the sides. Let rows wrap or stack to one column at phone width (about 400px). Give images and any `aspect-ratio` box `max-width: 100%`, and don't give anything a `min-width` wider than the screen. Only wide tables, code, and diagrams may exceed it; give each `overflow-x: auto` on its own container so the page body never scrolls sideways. The publish skeleton pads `:root` top and bottom by the phone's safe-area insets (zero everywhere except a phone app) so the page runs edge to edge while its content stays clear of the system bars; keep that padding. Put `<meta name="claude:viewport-fit-sides" content="cover">` at the top of the file beside your `<title>`: it promises that the side gutter uses those two `max()` paddings, so the tag goes in only together with both paddings, never alone. An edit of an older page that has neither leaves both out, unless the ask redoes the page's layout. With it the page also runs under a system bar at the phone's side. Anything fixed to a screen edge stays at `0` and adds that edge's inset to its own padding (one that spans the width takes the side gutter too); a floating or absolutely placed control adds the nearby edges' insets to its offsets. A sticky page header uses `top: env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px)` and never `0`. So that nothing scrolls into view above it, under the host's controls, paint that band with `body::before { content: ""; position: fixed; inset: 0 0 auto; height: env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px); z-index: 10; background: ... }`, in the header's own background where the header opens the page and in the page's where the sticky bar starts lower. Size a one-screen app with `height: 100%` on `html` and `body` instead of `100vh`, so it fits inside the `:root` padding. A page that includes its own viewport meta gets the `:root` padding only when that meta declares `viewport-fit=cover`. Use `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` wherever digits line up in columns.

**Make repeated elements consistent.** For cards in a row, label/value pairs down a list, or badges on sibling items, use the same edges, baselines, and inner padding on each, and put any recurring element in the same place on each. Let content set a container's height and pick a column count the items fill, so nothing stretches over empty space or sits alone in a row. Make text that can outgrow its track wrap or scroll in its own container; clipped text is a bug.

**Use card styling selectively.** Border, fill, radius, and shadow each mark an element as a separate object. Apply them by role, to set off the one element that needs it; applying the same radius and shadow to every block flattens the hierarchy. Open with big-number tiles only when those figures are the point of the page.

**Draw charts to scale.** Place marks, ticks, and labels with one scale, and make every label name a value the chart actually reaches. Color chart text from the theme tokens so it is readable in both themes. Keep marks, labels, and edges clear of one another and inside the drawing's bounds; in SVG, leave room in the viewBox for the outermost labels and give every drawn shape an explicit fill.

**Make the page complete at rest.** Everything meant to be read is visible once the page has loaded, with no scrolling to trigger it; that first still frame is what a thumbnail, a shared link, and a skimming reader all see. A section may animate in, but from a visible resting state, never left at `opacity: 0` waiting for an observer. Size a hero to its content instead of to the viewport; a `100vh` opener pushes the rest of the page out of that first frame. A tool or app opens in a realistic working state: the user's real data where it exists, otherwise example rows, a loaded sample, or a plausibly filled form, clearly marked as examples and never presented as the user's own figures. The first view shows what the tool does; an empty shell waiting for input shows nothing. When those records live in the `db` capability, keep them out of the page source. Its first frame renders before the store answers, so make that frame a designed empty state that names what will appear and how to add the first entry, then fill it from the store. Seed the store through the `ArtifactData` tool (what type instructions call `write_db`) after the first publish: the user's real data, or marked examples for a tool only the user will use. For a store other people will fill with their own entries, seed only what the user gave you or asked for, never invented people or records.

**Avoid AI-generated design.** AI-generated design currently clusters around a few looks: warm cream (#F4F1EA) with a serif display and terracotta accent; near-black with a lone acid-green or vermilion pop; broadsheet hairline rules with dense columns; a purple-to-blue gradient hero on white; Inter or Space Grotesk as the "safe" face; emoji as section markers; everything centered; `rounded-lg` everywhere; accent bar/rail on rounded cards. When the user specifies a visual direction, follow it exactly; their words always win, including when they ask for one of these looks. When nothing is specified, don't use that freedom on one of these defaults.

**Build cleanly.** Watch for overlapping elements, cascade collisions, and silent font fallbacks. Close every non-void element, double-quote attributes, give keyboard focus a visible state, and respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. Give every form control a stable `id` (the platform preserves form values, focus, and scroll position across a republish). For generative or decorative graphics, use Canvas or WebGL instead of hand-writing long SVG path data.

**CSS rules.** When writing the CSS, watch your selector specificity. It is easy to generate classes that cancel each other out, e.g. a type-based selector like `.section` and an element-based one like `.cta` both setting padding and margins between sections. Structure the cascade so it doesn't undo your spacing unnoticed.

**Writing the copy.** Treat words as design material and never as decoration. Write from the user's side of the screen: name things by what people recognize instead of how the system is built (a person manages *notifications*; they don't manage *webhook config*). Use active voice; a control states exactly what happens ("Publish", then a toast that says "Published"). Errors explain what went wrong and how to fix it, without apologies or vagueness. Prefer specific to clever. Write plainly, the way a knowledgeable person would talk. Avoid mannered devices: asides set off by em-dashes, "not X, but Y" framing, colon-then-reveal sentences, scare quotes around invented labels, and stock phrases such as "worth noting" or "honest caveat". Prefer short, direct sentences over compressed or clever phrasing.

**Name the page like a product; don't caption it.** The `<title>` is the artifact's name in the gallery and the browser tab, and it gives the reader a first impression of the care taken. Give the page a real name: a short noun phrase, typically two to four words, specific to the subject; or, for a page that exists to answer one question, that question itself, which then is the page's name. When the user already has a specific name for the thing, use that name for the title rather than coining a new one. Stop at the name; a title that adds its own explanation after a dash or colon reads as generated filler. The name must also identify the page among many: in the gallery it appears beside dozens of other artifacts, and a generic category label that could apply to any of them fails as a name just as an appended explanation does. When a candidate title combines the name with a generic word (a greeting, a category, a page-type label), keep the name; a trim that drops the identifying part and keeps the generic word produces a title that could apply to any page. This rule removes explanations and doesn't require brevity: a multi-word title that already reads as one specific name is finished, and shortening it further only makes it generic. Put the explanation in the one-sentence publish `description`; the gallery shows it directly under the title.

**Structure is information.** Structural devices (numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels) should encode something true about the content instead of decorating it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but those fit only if the content actually is a sequence, such as a real process or a typed timeline where the order is information the reader needs. Before adding numbered markers or similar devices, check that they actually make sense.

**When the page is a UI (dashboard, tool).** It is scanned and operated instead of read top to bottom, so the craft shifts from typography to information design. Put the summary before the detail. Encode state in form as well as in numbers (a pill, a chip, a severity stripe) so that whatever needs attention is visible at a glance. Semantic color (good / warning / critical) is separate from the accent hue and doesn't count as your accent. Give sparklines and charts the same care as type: an area fill, a faint grid, an emphasized endpoint. Interactive elements should look interactive.



## Process

Start from what the viewer should be able to do on the page, in addition to what they will read. If the page should take input, keep what people change for whoever opens it next, show live data, or ask Claude something, load the `artifact-capabilities` skill now and design around what it makes available to this user. A page that is only read doesn't need that.

Before writing the page, settle a short design plan (a compact token system) and write it into the file itself, as the `:root` block at the top of the page's `<style>`, rather than into your reply:
- **Color**: the palette as 4-6 named color tokens.
- **Type**: font tokens for 2+ roles: a characterful display face used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed.
- **Layout**: the layout concept as a one-line comment above the tokens.

Then build the rest of the page from those tokens, deriving every color and type decision from them. The plan is working material, not part of the answer: unless the user asks about the design, one plain sentence on the direction is the most to say about it, with no hex values or font names.

**Write, check once, publish.** Before publishing you may look at the rendered page once, where this session offers a way: one `ArtifactCheck` preview (or the Artifact tool's own `action: "preview"` where there is no separate `ArtifactCheck` tool), or else one screenshot of the local file; if the session offers none of these, skip the look. The preview renders desktop and phone widths in light and dark and lists overflow, colors that ignore the theme, blocked loads and console errors, including a script that fails to parse, so nothing it covers needs a check of your own. The look is optional: if you take it, make one pass of edits for what it shows, without a second look; then publish. For a page that charts real numbers, take the look rather than skip it, and spend it on the chart. A page whose point is logic (dates, money, scoring, parsing) may get one more check before publishing: one run of a pure function on a sample input, or, where no preview ran, one syntax check of its script; nothing more. A page that declares `capabilities` takes the look rather than skipping it, then one functional pass after the first publish, because the preview cannot run that code: read back once what the page stores or serves (one read of its stored data or one read-only route call; where that read alone would prove nothing, as on an empty store, you may first write one probe document yourself and delete it after the read, passing the `version` the write returned as `if_version`; no other test writes unless the user wants one), tell the user in one line what you exercised and what you could not, and stop. None of this becomes a loop, because the user is waiting for a link: no second screenshot, no scripts that probe the DOM, no re-running a check that passed. Review happens on the live page, and further polish is for the user to request; if the user reports something visibly broken (a clipped column, unreadable text, a control that does nothing), fix that, take at most one more look if the session offers a way, and republish once. These checks are for code you wrote into this page, not for content you fill into an Artifact made from an Artifact type (a Slides deck, a Design canvas): there the type's own instructions say whether to check, and if they say nothing, don't.

**Open viewers.** You don't need to do anything for viewers who already have the page open: published changes are delivered to them automatically at their next quiet moment, with state preserved where possible. If your page has state a viewer would miss (a game, a long form), register `window.claude?.hot?.snapshot(...)` and boot through `window.claude?.hot?.ready ? window.claude.hot.ready(start) : start(window.claude?.hot?.data ?? {})`; `hot` is the viewer's own update hook, not a capability behind `claude.use()`, and is absent outside a viewer, hence the `?.`.

## When the request is editorial

The stance changes here: the client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view. Make opinionated decisions, and take one real aesthetic risk where it serves the work.

Review the design plan against the subject before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page, revise that part in the plan itself, without narrating the revision to the user. Write the code only after the plan is specific to this subject, following the revised plan exactly.

**Principles** 

- The hero states the thesis: open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world (headline, image, live demo, interactive moment). 
- Typography sets the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, avoiding the families you would use on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design instead of a neutral container for the content. 
- Use motion deliberately. Think about whether and where animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. One orchestrated moment is usually more effective than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation adds to the impression that the design is AI-generated. 
- Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.
- Put your boldness in one place; keep everything around it quiet. If the accent clashes with the background, shift it toward an analogous hue or desaturate it instead of replacing it.

Where a first-time user gets stuck

I walked JusPrin’s first launch on every path I could reach and found {{COUNT}} places a newcomer is likely to misread or stall. Each orange number marks the spot on the screenshot; the same number below says what is on screen, why it confuses, and a proposed fix.

The proposals are mine and nothing is decided. The app freeze after Import is left out because another session is fixing it.

{{SECTIONS}}

How this was checked

  • A scratch copy of the current build ran with its own empty data folder and a copy of your OrcaSlicer folder. The welcome, the printer form, the OrcaSlicer list and Home after adding a printer are the real app.

content.text:
I went through JusPrin's first launch on every path I could reach and found 23 places where a newcomer is likely to misread something or get stuck. The report is at https://claude.ai/artifact/91wmdS3QU8UkzbPi1zog15. Each screen has numbered orange pins, and under it each problem has three parts: the words on screen, why they confuse, and a proposed fix. The fixes are only proposals; nothing in the app has changed.

**Your two points are in it.**
- **No sign-up.** The welcome has only "Continue with Google" and "Continue with email", with "New or existing account, same door." under them. I propose a "Sign up free" button with an "Already have an account? Sign in" link. Both would still send the same email code.
- **The credits line.** "Signed in as … · 500 credits" doesn't say the credits are new. I propose "You got 500 free credits for signing up."

**Bigger problems you didn't mention:**
- **The same credits have three names.** They're "Your first month: 500 credits" on the welcome, "500 credits" after signing in, and "First-month credits" on Home. That they expire first shows up on Home ("Expires 4 Dec").
- **Skip installs a Klipper printer.** "Skip for now" says files are sliced "for a generic 0.4 mm printer". The code actually installs OrcaSlicer's "Generic Klipper Printer", which has a 250 × 250 mm bed and writes Klipper G-code. A Bambu or Prusa owner who skips gets files that may not run on their printer, and nothing tells them.
- **The email step asks a new person for a password.** After typing an email, the card asks "How do you want to sign in?" and shows a Password box. The only hint that new users need the code instead is the smallest line on the card.
- **The OrcaSlicer import is all or nothing.** All eight printers come over with no way to leave one out. The screen doesn't say which printer JusPrin will use afterwards. "Start fresh" sounds like it erases something.
- **The printer step's Continue stays grey with no message.** After I picked a model it stayed grey for 84 seconds while the app read that printer's settings. My Mac was heavily loaded by other builds at the time, so a normal Mac is probably faster, but I didn't measure that.
- **The import result sounds alarming.** With one filament failed out of seven items, the title is "Some settings need attention". The failure line, "its base profile … isn't in JusPrin", uses jargon and gives no next step. "Retry failed items" will fail again for the same reason.

**One more freeze, separate from the import freeze.** Pressing Continue on the printer step froze the app for about 108 seconds while it installed the printer. It looks like the same kind of freeze as the one after Import, but I haven't checked that. You may want to pass it to the session fixing that one.

**How the screenshots were made:**
- The welcome, the printer form, the OrcaSlicer list and Home after adding a printer come from the real app, run from a copy of the current build with an empty data folder.
- The sign-in, signed-in and import-result screens are the real page, with the app's state set by hand. That way no accounts were created on staging, and I didn't have to run the import that freezes.
- Native windows aren't covered because I couldn't control the screen. That leaves out Preferences (opened by "Your own API key"), the folder chooser and OrcaSlicer's own dialogs.

The report is private, so others can open it only after you share it from the page's Share menu.

# First launch: fixes for 23 confusing spots (agreed by Kenneth, 2026-11-05)

Kenneth's words: "tell the coding agent to fix all the issues you identified, based on your recommendations".

The review with screenshots, each problem pinned where it appears:
https://claude.ai/artifact/91wmdS3QU8UkzbPi1zog15

Every item below is now agreed. The quoted new wording is the agreed direction; small wording changes to fit the layout are fine, but keep the meaning. Where an item says "check", find the real value before writing it; do not invent numbers. Follow the design-system rules for any new UI (tokens only), and keep `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` passing.

Most of this is in `HomeUI/src/components/Onboarding.tsx`, `AgentGroup.tsx`, `PrinterCard.tsx`, `PrinterPickerHost.tsx`, `AgentUI/src/components/BalancePanel.tsx` and `Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp` / `OrcaImporter.cpp`.

## Welcome screen

1. Sign-up, not only sign-in. Today the only buttons are "Continue with Google" and "Continue with email", with "New or existing account, same door." under them. Lead with signing up: the email button reads "Sign up free", with a small "Already have an account? Sign in" link. Both still send the same email code; only the words change. Remove "New or existing account, same door." Apply the same to Home's "Set up the agent" card (it uses the same SignInDoor).
2. Replace "Pick how the agent should think. Change it any time in Preferences › Agent." with what the choice is: "Sign up to use the AI agent, or skip it and just slice."
3. Replace "An Expert message is 5 credits." with what 500 credits buys in things the person does, for example "500 credits is about 100 questions to the agent". Check the number against the real per-message credit costs before writing it.
4. Fold "Your own API key — Free" and "Claude Code or Claude Desktop — Free · MCP server" into one quieter link, "Use your own AI account instead". The screen it opens explains both options. Drop "Free" (an API key is paid to the AI company) and "MCP server" from the welcome.

## Signing in

5. After the email is typed, the card asks "How do you want to sign in?" with a Password box and "Forgot password". Show only "Email me a 6-digit code" at first, with a small "Use a password instead" link that reveals the password box for people who set one. Drop "New here? The code makes your account." once the button itself says sign-up (item 1).
6. Code screen: replace "The sixth digit signs you in. Read the email on any device." with "Type the code from the email. You can open it on your phone."
7. Code screen: "Use the browser instead" becomes "Sign in with Google instead".
8. Google waiting card: "Finish signing in in your browser." becomes "Finish in your browser."

## After signing in

9. "Signed in as new@example.com · 500 credits" (welcome card for 1.5 s, and carried to the top of the printer step and the OrcaSlicer import screen) becomes "You got 500 free credits for signing up." with the email on a smaller line under it. Use the account's real credit total. Include the expiry (item 11).
10. (Same theme as 11 and 12, Home signed in.)
11. One name for the sign-up credits everywhere. Today: "Your first month: 500 credits" (welcome), "500 credits" (after sign-in), "First-month credits … Expires 4 Dec" (Home, from `lotName` for kind `signup` in BalancePanel.tsx, which the Agent panel shares). Use "free credits" in sentences and "Sign-up credits" as the row name, and say when they end in the sign-in line: "You got 500 free credits, good until 4 December." The welcome offer becomes "Sign up and get 500 free credits", with the one-month limit stated.
12. Home's account card "JusPrin account · Connected" becomes "Signed in as new@example.com". "Connected" stays printer language.

## OrcaSlicer import screen

13. A tick box per printer, all ticked to start. Only ticked printers are imported. Today all eight come over together.
14. Say which printer JusPrin will use after the import: "JusPrin starts with Bambu Lab P1S, the printer OrcaSlicer had selected." If that printer is unticked, name the one that will actually be selected.
15. "Start fresh" becomes "Choose my printer instead".
16. The folder line: "· 3 filaments" breaks onto two lines at the far right. Put "Also brings 3 filaments" on its own line, and the folder path in smaller text.

## Printer step

17. After a model is chosen, Continue stays grey with nothing on screen while the app reads that printer's settings (84 s in my run on a heavily loaded Mac; `printerForm.loading`). Show "Reading this printer's settings…" with a spinner under the nozzle buttons while it loads.
18. Remove "OrcaSlicer printers in another folder? Choose the folder…" from the printer step. It shows to everyone without an OrcaSlicer folder, including people who never used OrcaSlicer. File › Import › "Import from OrcaSlicer…" covers this.
19. "Skip, and JusPrin slices for a generic 0.4 mm printer until you add yours." is misleading: Skip installs OrcaSlicer's "Generic Klipper Printer" (Custom/machine/MyKlipper 0.4 nozzle: 250 × 250 mm bed, Klipper G-code), per `OrcaHomeBackend::assume_default_printer`. Say what the stand-in is: "Until you add yours, files are sliced for a 250 mm Klipper printer and may not print on other printers." Same fix for Home's "No printer yet" card and the drop-zone line that repeat it.

## Home

20. A printer added a moment ago says "Not connected. No network connection is set up." For a printer that has never had a connection set up, show "Connect it to send prints straight from JusPrin" beside the Connect button, with no status word. Keep the existing statuses for printers that have a connection.
21. Home's "Set up the agent" card never says why. Add one line at the top: "Get 500 free credits and ask the agent to fix failed prints."

## Import result screen

22. With 6 of 7 items imported, the title says "Some settings need attention". Use "Imported from OrcaSlicer" as the title and show the failure in its own row.
23. "Not imported · its base profile, Kingroon PLA Silk, isn't in JusPrin" becomes "This filament is built on Kingroon PLA Silk, which JusPrin doesn't have." Show "Retry failed items" only when a failure is one a retry can fix (a file that couldn't be read), not for a missing base.
24. Remove "OrcaSlicer's own files were not changed." The screen before already says OrcaSlicer keeps its own copy.

(Items 10 and 11 were one problem in the review; the review numbers 1–23 map to items 1–9 and 11–24 here.)

## Not in scope

- The freeze after Import is being fixed by another session. For whoever fixes it: pressing Continue on the printer step froze the main thread for about 108 s too, inside `SetupCommands::install_and_select_printer` → `Tab::select_preset` → `Plater::on_config_change` → `GLCanvas3D::reload_scene`. Probably the same cause; unverified.

## Done means

Each item checked on the real page, with a screenshot of each changed screen; the HomeUI and AgentUI tests and `wording.test.ts` pass; the C++ change for item 13 (ticked printers only) and item 23 (when Retry shows) has a test.

input.recap: Checked how the pricing and account pages connect to the app. Every "Get more credits" button opens the old v1 pricing page in the browser. The new v2 pricing page and Account section exist only as canvas designs, and the links between them are still undesigned.
input.ask: Should I design how the app, pricing page, checkout and plan management connect?

content.text:
Not me. Another session designed them, on the JusPrin v2 canvas: the pricing page in two versions (one for Obico Premium subscribers) and the Account section in Preferences in three. There is no separate subscription page in the design. I checked the app code and the server code, and the links between these pages are only half there.

**What the app does today**
- Every "Get more credits" button sends the person to the same address in their web browser, the server's `/ent/jusprin/pricing/`. The button appears in four places: the composer, the credits panel above the composer, the out-of-credits card in the chat, and Preferences › Account. The address is set in `Agent/AgentConfiguration.cpp:176` and opened in `Shell/ShellController.cpp:493` and `Preferences/PreferencesWindow.cpp:234`.
- That address still serves the **v1** pricing page, in `tsd-enterprise/web_ent/frontend/src/views/jusprin/JusPrinPricingPage.vue`. It offers Free and "JusPrin Unlimited" at $6.99 a month or $59.99 a year.
  - Its subscribe button opens Chargebee checkout.
  - For someone already subscribed, the button becomes "Manage Account" and opens Chargebee's customer portal, which is the nearest thing to a subscription page.
  - After a successful checkout it counts down and sends the person to `/jusprin/v1.0/embedded_chat/`, the v1 chat. That's a dead end for a v2 user.
- Preferences › Account in the app shows the plan name, the renewal date, credits and usage, and one "Get more credits" button. It has no "Manage plan" button.

**What is designed but not built**
- The pricing page has three cards: Pay as you go at $10 for 500 credits, Hobby at $10 a month for 750, and Workshop at $20 a month for 1,000. Obico Premium subscribers see $8 and $16. The design notes say checkout is Chargebee's hosted page.
- The Account section adds a "Manage plan" button with an outward arrow next to "Get more credits". The design never says where that button goes. My guess is the Chargebee portal, as v1 does, but nothing records it.

**Gaps nobody has designed yet**
- **Where you land after paying.** The v1 page sends people to the v1 chat. Nothing says what a v2 user sees after checkout, or how the app learns the balance changed.
- **Whether the browser knows who you are.** The pricing page knows the person only through a browser login. The app adds nothing to the address that identifies them. I haven't tried this, but from the code:
  - Someone who signed in with Google already went through the browser, so the page will probably know them.
  - Someone who signed in by email inside the app probably arrives signed out, and has to sign in again before they can buy.
- **Where "Manage plan" goes.** See the second point under "What is designed but not built".
- **Linking from the website.** No designed page on the website links back to the account or the app. The only links are the v1 page's "Back to Chat" and the redirect after checkout.
which session designed it?

The pricing page and the Account section were drawn in sessions titled "Draw the credits and plans screens on the canvas". There are three sessions with that title, and they share the same work, so the later two look like continuations or forks of the first:

- [Draw the credits and plans screens on the canvas](#local_d5f19660-2ce2-4962-af84-9891aabe1c55) — the earliest, last active 2 November.
- [Draw the credits and plans screens on the canvas](#local_b14d4c8e-5962-47f4-93d0-a36258ec6863) — also last active 2 November.
- [Draw the credits and plans screens on the canvas](#local_ff892f89-d364-4022-a2d9-d1de008d67d7) — the latest, last active 3 November. This is the one to ask about the designs.

The pricing decisions themselves came from [JusPrin pricing goals and priorities](#local_4d17825a-ac19-4732-a080-7e0c1dca6d1c). That is the session that started this one, and it lists those boards in its own notes. I found this by searching the session transcripts for the pricing page's board file and the drawing session's scratch folder. I haven't opened those sessions to read how they reached their decisions.

Okay, now let's integrate those pages into what you have designed so far. Take these into consideration, but not limited those. Use your own knowledge and experience as a good UX UI designer. Use the same principle as you did when you are doing the walkthrough to identify the confusing spot, design how the user should first encounter those pricing pages. Also think about where those each of those pages should live. My preference is as much as possible we want to give the cloud-related pages to the server to render, because updating these pages will be so much simpler than updating the app. However, we should have those pages rendered by the server have clear cut with a clear boundary with the pages rendered by the app so that maintaining backward compatibility won't be a nightmare.
I'll start by reading what the canvas already has for credits and pricing, so the new design builds on it rather than replacing it.

## 1a · First launch: Preferences › Agent over Home
The one setup flow, opened from Set up the agent over a first-run Home. The account row’s old line (“Free · sign in with your browser · nothing to install”) becomes the offer: the number is the headline, the one number on the screen and no dollars, and the button says what signing in gets. Key rows and the rest of the section are unchanged.

## 2a · The composer: model, thinking and credits ring, usage on hover
In a chat under way the model and thinking pickers keep their usual place and look, greyed, because a chat keeps its model (2c). Beside them, only a small ring of what is left, with no number and no animation. Hovering or tapping opens the total, then a bar for each kind of credit with what is left and its date, closest to expiry first, the way Claude’s and ChatGPT’s usage panels do it. Every credit pays for either tier, so the bars differ only by when the credits expire. A person with only their own API key sees no ring.

## 2b · A new chat: pick the tier before the first message
A chat keeps the model it starts with, so these pickers work only until the person sends their first message; after that they are greyed, as on 2c. The turn the app starts when a file opens runs on Expert for free and doesn’t fix the chat’s model. The JusPrin provider’s entries carry the price per message and one plain clause and name no model or vendor. Providers on the person’s own API key keep their model names with no price. A Standard chat has no thinking picker. For a Workshop subscriber the Standard option reads “Standard · 0 credits a message”. Default for a new chat is Expert while the first-month credits last. It is the existing model menu, with sections per provider, widened to 32

## 2c · A chat under way: greyed pickers, and a tooltip that says why and the price
Hovering either greyed picker says why it can’t change and what each message costs. On Standard the price reads “1 credit”, or “0 credits” for a Workshop subscriber. On the person’s own API key there is no price line. The design system’s tooltip is one line; this one needs two, so it would take a token change.

## 3a · Before the boundary: “About 25 credits left”
When the balance reaches 25 credits or fewer, on Standard as well as Expert, the composer says so once and the ring takes the warning colour, so the boundary is expected. Nothing else changes and sending works as usual.

## 3b · The next Expert message can’t be paid
Caught before sending. A chat keeps its model, so there is no Send with Standard: Send is disabled, one line says why, and there is one way forward. Get more credits opens the pricing page (5a), which says how packs and plans differ, so nobody has to choose between them from one line here. The typed text is untouched.

## 3c · The rare gateway 402: the failed-message card
Only a race between two sends reaches this. The card is the app’s .message-failure with the 402’s words and, as on 3b, only Get more credits. The message goes back into the composer, so nothing typed is lost.

## 3e · Picture in a Standard chat
The Standard model can’t see images, so the staged row’s second line is a warning that the photo won’t go with the message. Send stays enabled, because the words can still go on their own. Remove is the only action on the row. The picker option stays as short as on 2b.

## 4a · Preferences › Account, opened over Prepare
The window at its usual 640, over the screen it opened from, at the top of the section: the plan and Get more credits, the total, and a bar for each kind of credit. 4b shows the whole section.

## 4b · Account, the whole section: first month plus a pack
A bar for each kind of credit, as on Claude’s and ChatGPT’s usage screens, with what is left and when it expires. Bought credits get a bar like the others. Below, as on Lovable’s Plans & credit usage, usage per day with totals per chat, not a row per message. Hovering a bar shows that day. Purchases and rewards (4c) sit in the same list. The alert’s control is the Preferences checkbox the app already uses. Turns the app starts are free and don’t appear.

## 4c · Account on Workshop, an Obico Premium Subscriber
One bar, for the plan’s monthly credits; bought credits would add a second. Standard messages cost 0 credits, so they appear in Usage at 0 and there is no ceiling to count. The discounted price is shown as the price, detected, never entered.

## 5a · The pricing page, in the browser
Three cards named as decided, each stating its expiry rule in its own words. The one sentence at the top says what a message costs. Dollars belong here; Get more credits on the composer and in Account opens this page. The only other places that name dollars are the savings alert’s sums and the plan line in Account. The launch note is on the pack card with its end date (31 Jan is a placeholder for JUSPRIN_LAUNCH_DOUBLE_UNTIL). Checkout is Chargebee’s hosted page.

## 5b · The same page for an Obico Premium Subscriber
The discounted price is the price, $8 and $16, with one line saying why and no coupon to type. Pay as you go keeps its price: the discount is on subscriptions.

## 6a · First launch after the first month: what they have, not what they lost
A new chat starts on Standard, and free credits get the same ring as any other credits; hovering it shows Free credits, 50 of 50 left. No wall, no modal, no notice about what expired, no “upgrade”. A chat already on Expert stays on Expert, because a chat keeps its model, so it carries on from these credits and shows 3b once fewer than 5 are left.

## 6b · In a new chat, Expert is one click away and shows its price
The free credits pay for either tier, so Expert can be used from them. Picking Expert with too few credits is allowed: the composer then says “You have 0 credits; Expert needs 5 a message.” with Get more credits, and Send stays disabled. The menu stays open to Standard until the person sends their first message.

## 7a · Savings alert: Pay as you go to Hobby
Once, above the composer, dismissable, with the saving in dollars. On by default, with its switch in Preferences › Account. The sums are one tap away.

## 7b · The arithmetic, one tap away
The line opens in place to the one sentence of arithmetic. Nothing else moves and the person can keep typing.

## 8a · The print report button on the Print history entry
A report is about one G-code, so the button sits on that G-code’s entry, beside Print again and Export. It is not in the chat: by the time a print is done the person is usually in another chat, or back hours later, and can’t be expected to find the original one (Kenneth, 2026-10-27). No button while the print is running. An entry that was only exported has it too, because a print from a USB stick never reports back. One report per G-code.

## 8b · The report form, over Print history
Opens from the entry and names it, so the person knows which version they are reporting. Says what earns the reward: a photo of the printed object and a few sentences. The outcome is the person’s own answer for the report, not a print state: Print history stays without a failure state (decided 2026-10-27).

## 8c · After the report is sent
The button becomes a row on the entry, and that row is where the person sees the credits: this screen has no composer, so a “+25 credits” line there would go unseen. The row states that a report exists and nothing about how the print went.

## 8d · The way to the button from Home
People come back to Home with the part in hand, so the offer has to be visible before they open Print history. A project card gets the line when its latest G-code has finished and has no report; two weeks later the line goes away (my guess at the limit). It opens Print history filtered to that project. Home’s other ways in stay as the Print history page draws them. In a chat, the one-line G-code marker keeps its “history” link and gets no button.

## 9 · Model, thinking and the credits ring, state by state, light and dark
The composer’s new parts on their own, after the screens they live in. Toolbars are at the pane’s default width.

# Money pages: which the app draws, which the server draws (proposal, 2026-11-06)

Nothing here is agreed. Kenneth asked to put the pricing and plan pages into the first-run design, have the server render the cloud pages where it can, and keep a clear boundary so old app versions keep working.

Boards: canvas https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ, page "Credits & plans", from y=2900 (version 118). Builder: figma-mirror/tools/composer/build_money_page.py.

## The rule

The app shows credits; the server sells them. Anything with a dollar amount, a payment form or a plan change is a server page opened in the browser. The app never shows a dollar amount.

## Who draws what

App (ships with each release):
- Welcome and Home's agent card: the 500-credit offer, its scale line, a "See prices ↗" link.
- Composer: ring and balance panel, credit prices on the model picker, "About 25 credits left", the out-of-credits card, "+1,000 credits" after buying.
- Preferences › Account: signed-in line, plan name and renewal date (no price), a bar per kind of credit, usage per chat (needs local chat titles), savings-alert switch, "Get more credits" and "Billing ↗".
- Print history: the report button and "25 credits added".

Server (jusprinv2.obico.io):
- Credits and plans (pricing), signed in or out.
- Chargebee checkout, as today.
- Thank-you page (new; replaces today's redirect to the v1 chat at /jusprin/v1.0/embedded_chat/).
- Billing (new): plan in dollars, Change plan, Cancel plan, Chargebee portal for payment method and invoices, Delete account.
- The savings alert's sentence and sums.

## The contract between them (the only part old app versions depend on)

1. GET /v2/account, as today. Fields are only added, never renamed or removed; the app ignores fields it doesn't know. The app reads it again whenever its window becomes active, which is how "+1,000 credits" appears after paying.
2. New: POST /v2/web_link {page: "prices" | "billing", from: "welcome" | "composer_low" | "out_of_credits" | "preferences" | "alert"} → {url}. When signed in, the URL carries a one-time sign-in token (single use, about 60 s) so the browser opens as the app's account, whichever way the person signed in. Signed out, the URL has no token. The server answers these page names forever; an unknown name opens Credits and plans. Today the app builds the URL itself (AgentConfiguration.cpp cloud_pricing_url, gateway + "/ent/jusprin/pricing/"), so this replaces that.
3. The account answer's unused `suggestion` slot (web_ent/jusprin/ledger/account.py) carries {text, page}. The app shows the text as written and opens the page through a page link.

## Confusing spots this fixes

- After signing in with email in the app, the browser is probably signed out (unverified), so a person could buy on a different account. Fixed by the page link.
- "Pay as you go" shown as the plan of someone who never paid. Now "No plan".
- The pricing card said "500 credits" while its launch note said "$10 buys 1,000". The card now says 1,000 with "double the usual 500" under it.
- The pricing page showed neither balance nor current plan. Now a line at the top says both, and the current plan's button reads "Your plan".
- Nothing after paying said to go back to the app. The thank-you page does.
- The app's Account and a server account page would share a name. The server page is "Billing".
- Nothing defined where Manage plan went. It becomes "Billing ↗".
- An expired link lands on the signed-out pricing page with a line saying why, not an error.

## Server work this needs

- web_link endpoint and token sign-in (new).
- Pricing page v2 (the v1 page at /ent/jusprin/pricing/ offers Free and Unlimited $6.99).
- Thank-you and Billing pages.
- Moving the savings-alert arithmetic from the app into `suggestion`.

## App work this needs

- Call web_link instead of building the pricing URL.
- Refresh the account answer on window activation.
- Preferences › Account: "No plan", drop "$16 a month" and the discount line, "Billing ↗".
- Show `suggestion` when present.

content.text:
I've added ten new boards to the "Credits & plans" page of the canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ, version 118). They show which money pages the app draws and which the server draws, and how a person first reaches the pricing page. They sit below the existing pricing boards. The spec is at [money-pages-app-server-split-2026-11-06.md](money-pages-app-server-split-2026-11-06.md). Everything here is a proposal: nothing is approved and no code has changed.

**The split.** The app shows credits and the server sells them.
- **The app** draws the credit counts, the low and out-of-credits warnings, usage per chat, and a "+1,000 credits" line after buying.
- **The server** draws every page with a dollar amount or a payment form:
  - the pricing page;
  - Chargebee's checkout;
  - a new thank-you page;
  - a new Billing page, where you change or cancel a plan, reach payment method and invoices, and delete the account.

**What old app versions depend on.** Only three things cross between the app and the server:
1. **The account answer the app already reads.** The server may only add fields to it, never rename or remove them. The app reads it again whenever its window becomes active, which is how new credits appear after paying.
2. **A new page-link request.** The app asks for "prices" or "billing" and gets back a URL that signs the browser in as the same account, once, for about a minute. The server must answer those two names forever. A name it doesn't know opens the pricing page.
3. **An unused field in the account answer for server-written alerts.** The savings alert's text and sums would come from there, so new offers need no app release.

**How a person first meets prices:**
1. The welcome card says "Sign up and get 500 free credits", how long they last, and what comes after. A "See prices ↗" link opens the pricing page signed out, with "Sign in to buy" buttons.
2. Later, "Get more credits" opens the same page already signed in. A line at the top says the person's balance and which account the purchase goes to.
3. After checkout, the thank-you page says what was added and tells them to go back to the app.
4. Back in the app, the typed message is still in the box and Send is enabled.

**Confusing spots the design fixes:**
- **Wrong account.** After signing in with email in the app, the browser may open signed out (I haven't tested this). The person could then buy on a different account.
- **"Pay as you go" as a plan name.** Someone who never paid sees it as their plan. They now see "No plan".
- **500 or 1,000?** The launch-offer card said "500 credits" while its note said "$10 buys 1,000". The card now says 1,000.
- **Dead ends.** The pricing page didn't show the current plan, and nothing after paying said to return to the app.
- **Leftover v1 links.** The page after checkout today sends the person to the v1 chat, and nothing said where "Manage plan" goes. The first is replaced by the thank-you page, and "Manage plan" becomes "Billing ↗".

**Decision needed: should all dollar amounts move out of the app?** It's your call because it changes boards you've already seen. Two places in the app would lose their dollars:
- **The Workshop plan line** in Preferences › Account would lose "$16 a month" and the Obico discount line. They would appear on the Billing page instead.
- **The savings alert's dollar sums** would be written by the server instead of computed by the app.

If you approve, price changes never need an app release, but a person has to open the browser to see what they pay. If you don't, the account answer must carry prices and the app keeps formatting them. I recommend approving. Should all dollar amounts move out of the app?

**Decision needed: should the server build the one-time sign-in link?** This is new server work: one endpoint plus a short-lived, single-use sign-in token. Without it, the browser may be signed in as nobody, or as another account, when someone buys. The cheaper option is to always open the pricing page signed out and make people sign in again, which costs a step at the moment they want to pay. I recommend building the link. Should the server build it?

Separately: the fix list I sent the first-run coding session removes the "OrcaSlicer printers in another folder?" line from the printer step. You approved keeping that line on 2026-11-03, and your later "fix all the issues" reverses it. Say if you want it kept.
Let's discuss

Here's the trade-off as I see it, plus a middle option I should have offered the first time.

**What the boundary is really protecting against.** The risk isn't that a dollar sign appears in the app. The risk is that the app holds money logic: prices, discounts, the savings-alert arithmetic, how a plan is described. Once that logic ships, it's frozen in every installed version. If the Workshop price changes or the Obico discount ends, old apps keep showing the old number for months.

**What my proposal costs.** Someone on Workshop opens Preferences › Account and sees "Workshop, renews 1 Dec", but not what they pay. To find out, they click Billing ↗ and wait for a browser page. The savings alert loses its dollars too, and that alert was supposed to persuade with a dollar figure ("Hobby would have saved you $5.00").

**The middle option.** Instead of "the app never shows dollars", the rule could be "the app never works out or formats money; it shows text the server wrote". The account answer would carry a ready-made line such as "$16 a month · Obico Premium: 20% off". The app would print it as is. The savings alert works the same way through the unused field for server-written alerts. Price changes still need no release, because the app never knows what a price is. And the person still sees the price where they look for it.

What it costs is a small rule the server must keep forever: those lines are plain text the app shows without parsing. That's the same kind of promise as the page names, so it doesn't add a new kind of risk.

**What I'm unsure about.** I think Claude's and ChatGPT's apps show the plan name in their settings and send billing to the web, but I haven't checked, so treat that as a guess. I could look before you decide.

I now lean toward the middle option over my original rule. If you agree, I'll put the price line back on the Account board and the dollar figure back in the alert, both marked as server-written.

Which part do you want to dig into: where dollars may appear, the one-time sign-in link, or which pages the server owns?

input.recap: No technical reason forces an external browser. I defaulted to how the app opens the pricing page today. Two pricing decisions are open: how the launch offer works, and what to call buying credits once. Nothing on the canvas has changed yet.
input.ask: Should I redraw the boards with an in-app sheet, credit packs and a doubled first payment?

content.text:
**The external browser.** No technical reason forces it. I assumed it because "Get more credits" opens the default browser today, and I never questioned that. An in-app sheet is better for the person: they never leave the app, and the app sees checkout finish right away. It can close the sheet, add the credits and turn Send back on, with no "go back to JusPrin" step.

It also takes care of the wrong-account problem more simply. The app can open the sheet already signed in as its own account, so a one-time sign-in link is no longer needed for buying.

The app can already do this. It shows web pages inside its own windows on Mac, Windows and Linux, and the Agent pane and OrcaSlicer's Bambu login dialog both use them.

What an in-app sheet costs, as far as I could check:
- **Google sign-in doesn't work inside an app's web view.** Google blocks it on purpose ([Google's announcement](https://developers.googleblog.com/2021/06/upcoming-security-changes-to-googles-oauth-2.0-authorization-endpoint.html)). This only matters when someone is signed out. The welcome's "See prices" can show the prices and leave signing in to the app's own sign-in.
- **Chargebee's checkout inside a web view.** Chargebee supports this: it ships a wrapper that puts its checkout in a mobile app's web view ([Chargebee docs](https://chargebee.com/checkout-portal-docs/react-native-wrapper-for-mobile.html)). Its rule that digital goods must use in-app purchases is about iPhone and Android apps, not a desktop app downloaded from our site. What I couldn't confirm is whether the extra bank check some cards need (the one that pops up a bank page) works inside the sheet. We'd need to test that with a test card.
- **Saved cards (my guess, not tested).** Cards saved in Chrome and password-manager browser extensions probably won't fill in inside the sheet. An "Open in browser" link in the sheet covers people who want that.

**The launch offer.** You're right. Doubling only the one-time purchase makes it beat both plans. $10 would buy 1,000 credits that never expire, against Hobby's 750 a month that expire, so nobody has a reason to subscribe during the launch.

**Decision needed: what should the launch offer double?** My pick is to double the first payment of any choice: a one-time purchase gives 1,000, Hobby's first month 1,500, and Workshop's first month 2,000. The cost is capped at one payment per person, and the plans keep their edge. The alternative is to double every month of a plan until the offer ends, which costs more and pulls in people who only came for the bonus. What should the offer double?

**The name.** I'd call it a **credit pack**: "Credit pack · $10 once · 1,000 credits that never expire". It names a thing you buy and stands apart from the two plans. "Top-up" sounds like an add-on for people who already have a plan. "Buy credits" is fine as a button label but doesn't work as a card title. Someone who has bought packs but has no plan would read "No plan" in Account. Should the card be called "Credit pack"?

# Money pages: which parts the app draws, which the server draws (2026-11-06)

Boards: canvas https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ, page "Credits & plans", from y=2900 (version 121). Builder: figma-mirror/tools/composer/build_money_page.py.

## Agreed by Kenneth on 2026-11-06

- The server's pages open in a sheet inside the app, not in the browser.
- The one-time purchase is called "Credit pack".
- The launch offer doubles every credit amount until the end of January: a pack gives 1,000 instead of 500, Hobby 1,500 a month instead of 750, Workshop 2,000 instead of 1,000.

Everything below that is not in this list is a proposal.

## The rule (proposal)

The app draws credits. The server draws anything about money, inside a sheet the app owns. Where the app shows a price, it shows a sentence the server wrote and never works out a price itself.

## Who draws what (proposal)

App (ships with each release):
- **The sheet:** its frame, title, "Open in browser", close button, loading state and can't-load state. Never the page inside it.
- **Welcome and Home's agent card:** the 500-credit offer and a "See prices" link.
- **Composer:** ring and balance panel, credit prices on the model picker, "About 25 credits left", the out-of-credits card, "+1,000 credits" after buying.
- **Preferences › Account:** plan name with the server-written price line, a bar per kind of credit, usage per chat (it needs the chats' local titles), the savings-alert switch. "Get more credits" and "Billing" open the sheet.
- **Print history:** the report button and "25 credits added".

Server (jusprinv2.obico.io), shown in the sheet:
- **Credits and plans**, signed in or signed out.
- **Chargebee checkout**, as today.
- **Purchase done:** says what was added and to which account. Its "Back to your chat" button goes to the done address.
- **Billing:** plan in dollars, Change plan, Cancel plan, Chargebee's portal for payment method and invoices, Delete account.
- **Server-written lines:** the plan's price line and the savings alert.

## The contract (the only part old app versions depend on; proposal)

1. **GET /v2/account, as today.** The server only adds fields; the app ignores fields it doesn't know. One new field: the plan's price line, a finished sentence such as "$16 a month with Obico Premium's 20% off".
2. **POST /v2/web_link {page: "prices" | "billing", from}** returns a URL that signs in once as the app's account. The sheet opens it, and "Open in browser" asks for a fresh one. The server answers those page names forever; a name it doesn't know opens Credits and plans. Today the app builds the pricing URL itself (`AgentConfiguration.cpp`, `cloud_pricing_url`), so this replaces that.
3. **The done address, /v2/web/done.** When the sheet reaches it, the app closes the sheet and reads the account answer again. Checkout, a plan change and a cancel all end there. Closing with × also re-reads the account answer.
4. **The `suggestion` slot** in the account answer (`web_ent/jusprin/ledger/account.py`, unused today) carries the savings alert as {text, page}. The app shows the text as written.

## Constraints found

- **Google sign-in can't run inside a web view.** Google blocks OAuth in embedded web views on purpose. So the signed-out sheet's buttons read "Sign up to buy": they close the sheet and put the person on the app's own sign-up card. Source: https://developers.googleblog.com/2021/06/upcoming-security-changes-to-googles-oauth-2.0-authorization-endpoint.html
- **Chargebee supports its hosted checkout inside an app's web view.** It ships a React Native wrapper for exactly that. Its rule that digital goods must use in-app purchases applies to iOS and Android apps, not to a desktop app downloaded from our own site. Source: https://chargebee.com/checkout-portal-docs/react-native-wrapper-for-mobile.html
- **Unverified:** whether a card's bank check (3-D Secure) completes inside the sheet. Test with Chargebee's test cards before building.
- **Unverified:** browser-saved cards and password-manager extensions probably don't fill in inside the sheet. "Open in browser" covers that.

## Open

- The launch offer's edge case is my reading, not Kenneth's words: a subscription month billed on or before 31 Jan gets double.
- The proration line on Change plan is a placeholder for Chargebee's setting.
- Boards 5a and 5b (the old pricing page) and 4b's "Pay as you go" are superseded. A note on the canvas says so; their builder is unchanged.

content.text:
I redrew the money boards with your three decisions and published them to the canvas (version 121, the "Credits & plans" page, from y=2900). Images of all ten are posted above. Your decisions are applied everywhere:
- **In-app sheet:** the server's pages open in a sheet inside the app instead of the browser.
- **Credit pack:** the one-time purchase now has that name.
- **Launch offer:** every credit amount is doubled until 31 Jan.

**How the sheet works.** The app draws only the frame: a title, "Open in browser", the close button, and its own loading and can't-load screens (last image). Everything inside the frame is the server's page. Because the app owns the frame, a person never leaves the app. When checkout finishes, the server's page sends the sheet to a fixed "done" address. The app then closes the sheet, reads the balance again, and turns Send back on with the typed message still in the box.

**What a person sees, in order:**
1. The welcome card says "Sign up and get 500 free credits", how long they last, and what comes after, with a "See prices" link.
2. Before signing up, the sheet shows prices with "Sign up to buy" buttons. They send the person back to the app's own sign-up card, because Google sign-in can't run inside the sheet.
3. From the out-of-credits card, "Get more credits" opens the sheet already signed in. The line at the top says the balance and which account gets the credits.
4. After checkout, the sheet says "1,000 credits added" with a "Back to your chat" button.
5. In Preferences › Account, someone without a plan reads "No plan", and bought credits appear as "Credit packs". "Billing" opens the server's Billing page in the sheet, with plan, payment method, invoices and delete account.

**Launch offer on the cards.** Each card shows its doubled amount as the headline: the Credit pack 1,000, Hobby 1,500 a month, Workshop 2,000 a month. A note under each says "double the usual …". One rule is my reading, not your words: a plan month billed on or before 31 Jan gets double.

**Where the old pricing board sits.** It is still on the canvas, with a note beside it saying these boards replace it. The spec is at [money-pages-app-server-split-2026-11-06.md](money-pages-app-server-split-2026-11-06.md).

**Decision needed: should Account show the plan's price?** It's yours because it decides whether dollars appear anywhere in the app outside the sheet. In my proposal, the Workshop line in Account reads "$16 a month with Obico Premium's 20% off". The server writes that sentence, and the app only displays it, so a price change still needs no release. It costs one extra field in the account data that the server must keep sending in later versions. The alternative is no dollars in Account at all: the person opens Billing to see what they pay, and the server owes the app nothing extra. I'd keep the server-written line, because Account is where people look for what they pay.

Looks good. make the launch offer a bit more celebratory. 
Should Account show the plan's price as a line the server writes? - yes. but the info should be passed down from the server, not harcoded in the app.
also move the "delete account" to the account tab in preferences.

Making three changes: a more celebratory launch offer, the price line clearly coming from the server, and "Delete account" moved into Preferences › Account. Checking which colour tokens are available first.

items.content: Make the launch offer celebratory
Mark price line as server-sent
Move Delete account into Preferences
Render, publish, show here

content.text:
I've made all four changes and published them to the canvas (version 123, the "Credits & plans" page). Images of the changed boards are posted above.

**Launch offer.** Every pricing page now opens with a purple-to-pink banner with sparkles: "Launch celebration · Double credits on everything", and under it "Every credit pack, and every month of every plan, until 31 Jan". Each card has a pink "2× launch bonus" badge, with the usual amount struck through beside the doubled one: ~~500~~ 1,000 credits, ~~750~~ 1,500, ~~1,000~~ 2,000. After checkout, the confirmation carries a "Doubled for the launch" badge and says "A 500-credit pack, doubled for the launch." The colours come from the brand tokens.

**Price line.** Account's line "$16 a month with Obico Premium's 20% off" arrives from the server as a finished sentence in the account data the app already reads. The app has no price, discount or plan wording in its code.

**Delete account.** It's now the last group in Preferences › Account, with the design system's red danger button. Clicking it opens the app's own confirmation dialog. The server writes the dialog's sentence, so it can name the plan that ends and the credits that go. Confirming tells the server to delete the account, and the app then signs out. The server's page no longer has it.

**Usage.** The chart and the per-chat table moved to the server's page, now titled "Billing and usage". It holds the plan, payment method and invoices, credits left, and usage. In the app, the button in Account and "See usage" in the balance panel both open that page in the sheet. Account keeps the plan, the credit bars, the alert switch and Delete account.

**One gap: the server doesn't know chat titles today.** The server's account code (`web_ent/jusprin/ledger/account.py`) has a comment saying the gateway never sees a chat's title, so it names each usage row by chat id. The app gets its chat titles by asking the model through the same gateway, but the server doesn't keep that title answer. The simplest fix is for the server to save the title it returns for each chat. I haven't tried it; it's work for whoever builds the Billing and usage page.

The spec is updated at [money-pages-app-server-split-2026-11-06.md](money-pages-app-server-split-2026-11-06.md). It lists what you've agreed to separately from what is still my proposal.

content.text:
**Chat titles: you didn't miss anything, and your idea is better than mine.** Here's the issue in one case. Someone opens Billing and usage and sees a row: "19 Nov · Expert · 40 credits". The chat column needs a name like "Resizing a Print to Fit the Bambu A1 mini". The server only knows the chat's id, because titles live in the app. Your fix works: the app sends the chat's current title with each request, and the server stores it beside the chat id.

It also handles a case mine didn't. People can rename a chat in the app, and the app's chat code does have a rename action. With your approach the newest title wins, so a renamed chat shows its new name. Two small details whoever builds it should handle:
- **The first message** goes out before the chat has a title. The row fills in with the next request.
- **Older app versions** send no title, so their rows need a fallback such as "Untitled chat".

I've put this on the Billing and usage board and in the spec.

**What changed on the canvas** (version 125; images above):
- **The Credit pack card** has two tick boxes above its Buy button.
  - "Auto-reload: buy another pack when I drop below 50 credits": off until the person ticks it, and charged to the card used for the pack.
  - "Tell me if a plan would have cost me less": on by default, and shown once above the message box. The person now sees every way to pay on one card.
- **For a Hobby subscriber**, the same card shows auto-reload already on.
- **Billing and usage** has a row "Auto-reload is on" with Change and Turn off buttons. It explains that a pack costs $10, gives 1,000 credits during the launch, and is bought whenever the balance drops below 50.
- **Preferences › Account** no longer has the Alerts group. It shows the plan, the credit bars and Delete account.

The spec at [money-pages-app-server-split-2026-11-06.md](money-pages-app-server-split-2026-11-06.md) lists these as agreed.

**Decision needed: when should auto-reload buy a pack?** I drew "below 50 credits" as a placeholder. The pack is the only thing auto-reload buys, $10 for 500 credits (1,000 during the launch). At 50, about 10 Expert messages are left when the purchase happens, so the person never hits the out-of-credits card mid-chat. A lower number, such as 10, charges later but risks a message that can't be paid while a card payment is still being approved. A setting the person chooses adds a control to the card. I'd keep a fixed 50.
Pick another

What number should it be? Here's what each choice means, so you can set it in one reply:

- **25 credits.** The composer already says "About 25 credits left" at that point. Auto-reload would buy at the same moment, so someone with auto-reload on would see "+500 credits" where they'd otherwise see the warning. About 5 Expert messages are left when the card is charged.
- **10 credits.** The charge comes as late as possible, and 2 Expert messages are left. If the card is declined or the payment is slow, the next message may not be payable.
- **100 credits.** About 20 Expert messages are left, so there's lots of room for a slow or declined card. Someone who stops using JusPrin can still be charged with plenty of credits unused.

Tell me the number and I'll update the Credit pack card, the Billing and usage row and the spec.
10 credits

content.text:
Above are all eleven boards as they are on the canvas now (version 127), in the order a person meets them:

1. **The map:** what the app draws, what the server draws, and the five things that pass between them.
2. **The welcome:** "Sign up and get 500 free credits", with a "See prices" link.
3. **Prices before signing up:** in the sheet over the welcome, with "Sign up to buy" buttons.
4. **Prices from the out-of-credits card:** the launch banner, and the Credit pack card with auto-reload (below 10 credits) and the savings alert.
5. **Checkout finished:** "1,000 credits added", with the "Doubled for the launch" badge.
6. **Back in the app:** "+1,000 credits", Send turned back on, and the typed message still there.
7. **Preferences › Account:** No plan on the left, Workshop with the price line from the server on the right. Each has Delete account at the end.
8. **Billing and usage:** the plan, payment method, credits, auto-reload, and usage per day and per chat.
9. **Change plan, on Hobby:** "Your plan" is marked, Workshop's button reads "Switch to Workshop", and auto-reload is on.
10. **Delete account:** the confirmation dialog over Preferences › Account.
11. **The sheet's own states:** loading, and the server can't be reached.

Can we insert a blank <div> on the app's account page so that it displays whatever the server passes back, either as part of the account api call, or as a separate api? the div sits near the top of the account page, and is usually hidden when the server doesn't pass back anything.  What I'm thinking about is to have the launch offer promotion shown there as the <div> block during the promotion period.

Yes, the app can do this. There's one choice to make first: whether the server sends words or a whole page. Take the launch offer as the example. Alex opens Preferences › Account in January and sees the purple "Double credits on everything until 31 Jan" block above their plan, with a "See the offer" button that opens Credits and plans in the sheet. In February the server sends nothing and the block disappears. The space is hidden when the server sends nothing, when it's offline, or when the app is on someone's own API key. It never delays the rest of the page.

**Decision needed: what does the server send for that block?**

- **Words, which the app lays out.** The account data the app already loads gets one more field. It holds a small label ("LAUNCH CELEBRATION"), a headline, a sentence, a button label with a page name, and a style name such as "celebrate". The app draws it with its own design-system parts, including the gradient and sparkles from the pricing page. It shows up at the same moment as the rest of Account, because it arrives with the same data. Nothing from the server runs inside the app.
  - Cost: the server can change the words, dates, button and destination any day, but not the layout. A new shape, such as a picture or a countdown, needs an app release, and only new app versions would show it.
- **A small server page shown in a box.** The block is a sandboxed frame showing a page the server serves. An empty answer keeps it hidden. The server can change anything at any time, including pictures and layout. This is the closest to "a blank div that shows whatever the server passes".
  - Cost: it loads after the page around it, so it pops in a moment later and has to tell the app its height.
  - Cost: it has to be locked down. The app's web pages carry a channel that can call into the native app. I haven't checked whether that channel also reaches a frame inside the page. Ruling that out is a must before building.
  - Cost: the server has to copy the app's colours and fonts itself to look like the rest of Account.
- **A piece of HTML dropped straight into the div.** It looks quick, but I'd avoid it. The app would have to strip anything that could run. The HTML would also style itself with the app's CSS class names, so those names quietly become part of the contract. Rename a class and old banners break.

I recommend words that the app lays out, at least for the launch. The launch block is words and a button, and this way it can't break, can't flicker and can't reach into the app. If you expect promotions with pictures or unusual layouts later, the server page is the better long-term choice, once the native-channel question is checked.

Both options fit the contract we already drew. The block is one more server-written item, next to the plan's price line and the delete warning. Its button opens a page through the same page-link request the sheet uses.

Which do you want the server to send: words, or a page? Tell me and I'll draw the block on the Account boards.

- Chargebee supports its hosted checkout inside an app's web view (it has a React Native wrapper). Its in-app-purchase rule applies to iOS and Android apps only.
- Unverified: whether 3-D Secure card checks complete inside the sheet, and whether saved cards or password managers fill in there.

**The contract between app and server (proposal):**
1. GET /v2/account, additive only. It gains a plan price line and a delete warning as finished sentences. DELETE /v2/account deletes the account.
2. POST /v2/web_link {page: prices | billing, from} returns a one-time signed-in URL. The server answers these page names forever; an unknown name opens Credits and plans. This replaces today's `cloud_pricing_url` in `AgentConfiguration.cpp:176` (gateway + "/ent/jusprin/pricing/").
3. The done address /v2/web/done: when the sheet reaches it, the app closes the sheet and reads the account answer again.
4. Server-written lines arrive in the account answer's `suggestion` slot (`web_ent/jusprin/ledger/account.py`, currently 'suggestion': None).

content.text:
I've drawn the server's box near the top of Preferences › Account (it's on the canvas now, and I sent you the screenshot). Before anyone builds it, there's a security problem to fix.

**How it looks.** Say Alex has no plan and opens Account in January. Under the "Account" heading they see a purple "Launch celebration" box: "Double credits on everything", "Credit packs and every month of every plan, until 31 Jan", and a "See the offer" button. A Workshop subscriber opens the same page and the server sends them nothing, so there's no box and no gap.

**How it would work (my proposal):**
- The account data the app already loads gets one optional field: the URL of the server's small page. If it's missing, the box stays hidden. It also stays hidden when the app is offline or using the person's own API key.
- The app puts that page in a locked-down frame. The frame stays hidden until the server's page has loaded and reported its height, so an empty or half-loaded box never shows.
- The frame can send the Account page only two messages, and only from our server's address:
  - its height;
  - "open prices" or "open billing", which opens that page in the sheet.
- The Account page drops any other message. Those two messages are all that old app versions rely on. Everything inside the box can change any day without an app release.

**The security problem.** I checked the question I flagged last time. The app's link to its native side does reach a frame inside the page.
- On macOS, wxWidgets adds that link to every frame in the page, not just the main one. When a message comes in, it doesn't tell the app which frame sent it.
- I tested this with a bare macOS web view set up the way wxWidgets sets one up. A sandboxed frame from another site sent a message, and the native side received it.
- On Linux, the wxWidgets source does the same. I haven't checked Windows.
- So as things stand, a page inside the box could send the same commands as the Account page itself, such as sign out.

**The fix I propose.** It's all in JusPrin's own code; nothing in the wxWidgets dependency changes. Each time the Account page loads, the app hands it a secret. It does this by running a script, and that script only runs in the main page, never in a frame. The app then ignores any message to its native side that doesn't carry the secret.

The sheet I proposed for showing the server's pages needs similar care. The app's usual way of creating a web view always adds this link, so the sheet needs a web view created without it.

All of this, including the leak and the fix, is in `money-pages-app-server-split-2026-11-06.md` (untracked). The board is version 129 of the canvas: https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ.

Let's assume we don't have any active links or buttons inside this page. For this one, we can say sign up today without a link, right? We can even program the server to check for the account status and if the user has already signed up and subscribed or paid, the server can just return none, right?

content.text:
Yes to both. With no links or buttons, the box is just words and pictures, so it can say "Sign up today" as plain text. The server can also check the person's account and send nothing to anyone who has subscribed or bought a pack. And with nothing to click, the security problem goes away.

**Why the security problem goes away.** The box has no buttons, so the frame it sits in can run with scripts turned off. A page that runs no scripts can't send anything to the app. I tested this on the same bare macOS web view as last time, with scripts off in the frame. The frame's script never ran and nothing reached the native side. The Account page could still measure the frame's height, so the app can size the box itself and show it only once it has loaded. We no longer need the secret-per-page fix for this box.

**One catch: signed-out people.** The account data the app already loads needs the person to be signed in. So the box needs its own small request, which is your "separate API" option. The app sends that request with the sign-in token when it has one, and without it otherwise. The server then picks what to send:
- **Signed out:** "Sign up today. Until 31 Jan, every credit pack and every month of every plan gives twice the credits." The app's own sign-up button sits just below it.
- **Signed in but never paid:** the same offer, without "Sign up today". The app's "Get more credits" button is in the plan card below.
- **Subscribed or bought a pack:** nothing, so there's no box and no gap.

**What the server can and can't do with the box.**
- The server sends the box as ready-made HTML, or sends nothing. Old app versions only rely on that.
- Text and wording can change any day.
- The box can't use the app's styles, so the server's HTML has to carry its own colours and fonts.

I redrew the Account board with all three people side by side and sent you the screenshot. It's version 131 of the canvas: https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ. The spec, `money-pages-app-server-split-2026-11-06.md`, now describes the box this way.

The sheet that shows the server's full pages still needs its own fix. The app's usual way of making a web view always gives it a line to the native side, so the sheet must be built without one.
