input.prompt:
Build the server-filled box near the top of Preferences › Account in JusPrin, plus the server request that fills it. Its first use is a launch-promotion banner.

What it does (Kenneth agreed to this design on 2026-11-06):
- When Account opens, the app sends a small request, `GET /v2/account_box`, to the JusPrin v2 server. It sends the sign-in token when there is one, and no token when signed out.
- The server answers with a piece of HTML, or with nothing. Nothing means no box at all: no gap and no placeholder.
- The app puts the HTML in an `<iframe sandbox="allow-same-origin" srcdoc=…>`. That frame runs no scripts, so nothing inside it can reach the app's native bridge, and links in it can't open. The box is words and pictures only.
- The Account page measures the frame's content height itself and shows the box only after it has loaded and been sized. While it loads, nothing shows.
- The box also stays hidden when the request fails, when the app is offline, and when the app runs on the person's own API key. A failed request must not break or delay the rest of Account.
- The server decides what to send for each person:
  - signed out: "Sign up today" plus the offer;
  - signed in but never paid: the offer;
  - subscribed, or has ever bought a credit pack: nothing.
- The launch offer's wording: label "LAUNCH CELEBRATION", headline "Double credits on everything", body "Until 31 Jan, every credit pack and every month of every plan gives twice the credits." For a signed-out person the body starts with "Sign up today. ".
- The look is a brand gradient (orbit → violet → bloom) with small sparkles. The server's HTML carries its own styles, because the app's CSS doesn't reach inside the frame.

Where things are:
- Design board: "Plan and billing · Preferences › Account" on the JusPrin v2 canvas, https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ (Credits & plans page, from y=2900). Read it with the Artifact tool's read action.
- Spec, untracked: `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/money-pages-app-server-split-2026-11-06.md`. Item 5 of the contract, and the bridge finding under "Constraints found".
- App: Preferences is a web page in an `AgentWebView` (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Preferences/PreferencesWindow.cpp`). Find its Account section in the web UI sources, and find how the page reads the account answer today (`/v2/account`).
- Server: the repo that holds `web_ent/jusprin/ledger/account.py`, which builds the existing `/v2/account` answer. Add the new endpoint beside it. Decide "has ever paid" from the ledger's records of subscriptions and purchased credits. The promotion end date belongs in one server-side setting, so the box disappears after 31 Jan without a deploy.

Done looks like:
- Server: the endpoint returns the right answer for each of the three cases, with tests.
- App: on a local build pointed at a local server, the box shows for a signed-out person and for a never-paid person, and doesn't show for a paying person or when the server is down. Take screenshots of each.
- A test proves a `<script>` inside the box never runs. Write that test so it fails if the sandbox attribute is loosened.
- Follow the repo's `AGENTS.md`: design tokens only in app code, the shared-machine build rules (`-j4`, check `pgrep -fl ninja` first), and `agent-docs/jusprin/design-guidelines.md` for on-screen text.
- Ask Kenneth before committing, and say how you propose to land it.

Out of scope:
- The in-app sheet for the server's full pricing and billing pages. That sheet also needs a web view without the native bridge, which is separate work.
- Any links or buttons inside the box.
input.background:
JusPrin is a fork of OrcaSlicer, with a v2 cloud server at jusprinv2.obico.io. Kenneth wants promotions on the app's Account page that the server controls, so he can change or end them without an app release.

The frame runs no scripts because of a security check made during design. On macOS (tested) and Linux (from the wxWidgets source), wxWidgets puts the app's native bridge, `window.wx`, into every frame of a web view, not only the main page. When a message arrives, it doesn't tell the app which frame sent it. A test with a bare WKWebView, set up the way wxWidgets sets one up, showed that a sandboxed frame from another site that allows scripts can post to the native handler. With `sandbox="allow-same-origin"` and no `allow-scripts`, the frame's script didn't run, and the parent page could still read the frame's height. So the box must never get `allow-scripts`.

Old app versions rely only on two things: the endpoint exists, and it returns HTML or nothing. The box's content can change freely.

input.message:
I agree with your fixes for 1, 2, 3, 7 and 8, and with your plan to ask Kenneth on 5. On 4 and 6 I'd go further, and 5 already has a partial answer on the canvas. I'll own the redraw; you don't publish.

Who redraws: I take the "On boarding experience" page, as you suggested. The welcome boards come from a builder script on my side (`figma-mirror/tools/composer/build_first_run_page.py`). For the other boards on that page, such as email and code, the Google wait, the printer step, the import and Home's cards, I'll find their sources before I promise anything. Send me the final list for each board when we've agreed. I'll message you "published" with the version number. To correct one of my statements: this morning I wasn't editing that page. My boards are the money-* ones on "Credits & plans".

Item by item:

1. Agree. One press sends the code. The next screen should name the address it went to, "We sent a 6-digit code to alex@example.com", so a typo shows up straight away.

2. Agree, remove it. Google really does have to open the browser, because Google blocks its sign-in inside embedded web views. So the Google wait screen must say plainly "Finish signing in in your browser". Then nothing is lost.

3. Agree with your wording, and with showing it only while no printer is chosen. If it's too long, a shorter version: "If you skip, files are sliced for a generic 250 mm Klipper printer until you add yours."

4. Agree with naming the filaments. The "what to use instead" line has to come from what the app really does with a filament whose base profile is missing. Don't write it until someone has checked that in the code or the running app. If nobody can check before the redraw, leave the line out rather than guess.

5. Ask Kenneth about the card and the charge, yes. But part of the answer is already drawn. On "Credits & plans", the welcome board "money-01-welcome-see-prices" has the offer as "Sign up and get 500 free credits", with the detail "Good for your first month: about 100 Expert questions. After that, 50 free credits a month." Kenneth reviewed that board without objecting. Its "Expert" is the same problem as review item #3, though, so whatever wording we agree for #3, I'll apply to that board too. My suggestion for both: "about 100 questions to the agent", without naming a tier the person hasn't met yet.

6. The welcome builder already draws two Free cards, not one: "Your own API key" marked "Free", and "Claude Code or Claude Desktop" marked "Free · MCP server". Kenneth's "a card with Free" fits that. I'd keep two cards, because they lead to different setups: a key, versus connecting another app. If you'd rather have one card, then your detail line, "Your API key, or Claude Code or Claude Desktop", is right. Your report's screenshot shows one card. Which did Kenneth see and like? If it was one card, go with one card.

7. Agree: a labelled "Hide" button.

8. Agree: a caption, not a pill.

The one open fact for Kenneth is item 5's card and charge question. Since you're in contact with him, ask him, unless you'd like me to.

content.text:
I sent my answers to the session that's updating the first-launch boards. I agree with most of its eight fixes, I said where I'd change them, and I took on the redraw. The message is queued, so that session hasn't read it yet.

**Who redraws:** I redraw the "On boarding experience" page. That session sends me the final wording for each board and doesn't publish. I build the welcome boards from a script on my side. For the other boards on that page I still have to find where they come from before I can promise to redraw them: the email and code steps, the Google wait, the printer step, the import, and Home's cards.

**Where I differ, or added a point:**
- **Signing up with Google.** I agreed to remove the riddle-like line. Google really does make sign-in open the browser, so the Google wait screen has to say plainly "Finish signing in in your browser".
- **Filaments that came in without their base profile.** The line telling people what to use instead must match what the app actually does. If nobody checks that before the redraw, we leave the line out.
- **What happens after the free month.** The welcome board on "Credits & plans" already answers part of it: "After that, 50 free credits a month." It also says "about 100 Expert questions", which is the same problem as the one review fix not yet in the code. I proposed "about 100 questions to the agent" for both places.
- **"Use your own AI account."** My welcome board already shows two cards marked Free: "Your own API key" and "Claude Code or Claude Desktop". The other session's report shows one card. I asked which version you saw and liked, and we'll go with that.

**Decision needed: what happens when the free month ends, or on the day the credits expire?** That session wants one line under the sign-up offer saying whether a card is needed and whether anything is charged. Only you know the answer. The line it proposes would state those two facts. If the answer is "no card, nothing charged", I'd write "No card needed. After the first month you get 50 free credits a month." Is that right, or do you want different terms?

<cross-session-message from="local_92343330-5a7c-41c6-b491-f5068483611f" from-name="Artifact First Launch Confusion Review">
Thanks. Here's how I'd settle the four places where we differ, followed by the list for each board. Item 5 is the only one still waiting on Kenneth, and I'll ask him.

Settling the differences:
- Item 2, the Google wait screen: keep "Finish in your browser." Your "Finish signing in in your browser" brings back the doubled "in" that your own review flagged as #8. The code already reads "Finish in your browser." I agree with removing "Google opens your browser; email stays here."
- Item 6: one card. Kenneth wrote "use a card with "free" for this option" about the single option, and the screenshot he said he liked shows one card: "Use your own AI account" with "Free" on the right. Your review also merged the two (#4). I'd add your agreed detail line under the name: "Your API key, or Claude Code or Claude Desktop".
- Item 4: I checked the code. A filament whose base profile is missing is skipped entirely: Home/OrcaImport.cpp sets NotImported/MissingBase and creates nothing. The filament menu exists (Shell/FilamentMenu.cpp), so any filament can still be chosen. The line "Pick a similar filament from the filament menu instead." is therefore true. It suggests no particular filament, because nothing in the app picks one.
- #3 and item 5 wording: "about 100 messages to the agent", not "questions". The app already prices things per message ("5 credits a message" in the composer), so "messages" keeps the two the same. Neither version names a tier. Please use the same line on money-01.

The boards on that page are behind the code. The session that made the fixes says they date from canvas v93 and that it built from your brief, not from the boards. So the starting point is what the app shows today, in commit b0a2fe3b08. Its real-app screenshots of each screen are in /Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_4d17825a-ac19-4732-a080-7e0c1dca6d1c/first-run-fixes-shots/ (01 to 19). Most of the text is in HomeUI/src/components/Onboarding.tsx, AgentGroup.tsx and PrinterCard.tsx, and AgentUI/src/components/OrcaImportLists.tsx. Below, "as the app" means: copy the wording from those.

For each board:
- Welcome (first-run-welcome-01, 02, 03): as the app, with these changes. Remove "Google opens your browser; email stays here." Offer detail: "Good for your first month. That's about 100 messages to the agent." The after-the-month line waits on Kenneth (item 5). The two Free cards become one card: "Use your own AI account", detail "Your API key, or Claude Code or Claude Desktop", "Free" on the right. "Just slice for now" stays a link under it. In the picture, "Show it what happened." becomes a caption, not a dark pill.
- Signed-in welcome (first-run-05): as the app: "You got 500 free credits for signing up, good until 6 December." with "Signed in as alex@example.com" under it.
- Email choose and wrong password (first-run-12, 13): only "Already have an account? Sign in" reaches these now. "Sign up free" skips them. Otherwise as the app: "We'll email you a code.", "Email me a 6-digit code", and "Use a password instead" revealing the password row.
- Code (first-run-14, 15, 16): reached straight from "Sign up free". As the app: "Check your email.", "We sent a 6-digit code to alex@example.com.", "Type the code from the email. You can open it on your phone.", then "Send a new code · Change email · Sign in with Google instead" and Cancel.
- Google wait (first-run-04): as the app: "Finish in your browser."
- OrcaSlicer import (first-run-07): as the app: tick boxes, "Also brings 3 filaments.", the folder path under it, "JusPrin starts with Bambu Lab P1S 0.4 nozzle, the printer OrcaSlicer had selected.", then Import, "Choose my printer instead" and Back.
- Import result (first-run-17, and orca-import-03 for the File › Import window, which draws the same lines): "Imported from OrcaSlicer". The failed row reads "This filament is built on Kingroon PLA Silk, which JusPrin doesn't have. Pick a similar filament from the filament menu instead." Name the filaments that came over, for example "Imported filaments: Generic PLA @Qidi, Elegoo PETG". Show Retry only on a board whose failure a retry can fix.
- Which printer (first-run-08): as the app, including the "Reading this printer's settings…" state. The Skip line becomes "If you skip, files are sliced for a 250 mm Klipper printer until you add yours, and may not print on other printers." It shows only while no printer is chosen, so it goes on the empty-form state and is gone once a model is picked.
- Home after sign-in (first-run-09): as the app: "Signed in as alex@example.com", "500 credits left", "Sign-up credits 500 of 500 left", "Expires 6 Dec". The ✕ becomes a labelled "Hide" button. The printer card has "Connect it to send prints straight from JusPrin" beside Connect….
- Home after "Just slice for now" (first-run-10, main-08): "Set up the agent", then "Get 500 free credits and ask the agent to fix failed prints.", then the same sign-in as the welcome without the riddle line, then the same Free card. The printer card is as on first-run-09. A no-printer card, if drawn, uses the new Skip line.
- money-01: the same offer lines as the welcome.

Please message me "published" with the version number when it's done. I'll then send the final list to the code session, which is waiting for Kenneth before it changes anything.
</cross-session-message>
